questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
‘An increase in consumption by one person leaves the benefits available to others undiminished’. Which good does this statement define?

options.A: a demerit good
options.B: a merit good
options.D: a public good

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a production possibility curve for a farmer. The original position is X. If the farmer switches some of his land from producing pears to producing apples, which point represents his new position? pears A D X B C O apples

A student buys a flute for $80 but then is unable to learn to play it. It has a resale value of $50, while the shop retail price of the same type of flute has risen to $95. What is the present opportunity cost to the student of keeping the flute?
The diagram shows a supply curve for beef. S price O quantity What explains why the supply curve for beef slopes upwards?

options.A: An increase in the demand for beef will bring about an increase in supply.
options.B: Farmers’ productivity rises as the price rises.
options.C: Increased production leads to a reduction in costs.
options.D: The cost of additional beef production rises as output increases.

questions.questionText: A theatre increases the price of its tickets from $10 to $15. As a result, its total receipts decrease from $10000 to $6000. Within what range does the price elasticity of demand for theatre tickets lie?

A taxi firm raises fares at its busiest times by as much as five times the normal fare. Taxi drivers and customers are notified of the changes by mobile (cell) phone. What will result from this policy?

options.A: It will be less likely that there is a market equilibrium.
options.B: Potential customers will have less perfect information.
options.C: The market surplus will become a shortage.
options.D: The supply of taxi rides will become more price elastic.

questions.questionText: The table shows Shanaz’s and Sunil’s price elasticity of demand for restaurant meals and theatre tickets. Shanaz Sunil restaurant meals –0.8 –1.2 theatre tickets –1.3 –0.7 There is a rise in the price of restaurant meals and a fall in the price of theatre tickets. What can be concluded after these price changes?

options.A: Restaurant owners will receive more income.
options.B: Shanaz will spend more money on both theatre tickets and restaurant meals.
options.C: Sunil will spend more money on both theatre tickets and restaurant meals.
options.D: Theatre owners will receive less income.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a normal product. price W X demand Y Z O quantity Which two points indicates a move from a price inelastic point to a less inelastic point?

options.A: W to X B X to W C Y to Z D Z to Y

options.A: At price OP , UV represents the market surplus.
options.B: At price OP , P X represents the quantity that consumers would like to buy.

Producer surplus is the difference between

options.A: the consumer surplus from the good and the producers’ total cost of supplying the good.
options.B: the highest price that the consumer would be willing to pay for the good and the price the producer actually sold it for.
options.C: the lowest price that the producer would accept for the good and the price the producer actually sold it for.
options.D: the quantity that the producers manufacture in a week and the amount sold to consumers in that week.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to raise the incomes of farmers without raising the price of food to consumers. Which policy should it use?

options.A: a maximum price below the market price for food
options.B: a minimum price below the market price for food
options.C: a payment of a subsidy to farmers to produce food
options.D: a release of government food stocks onto the market

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply of rice. Supply increases from S to S .
Money is paid by the government to an unemployed worker in the form of a benefit. Why is this called a transfer payment?

options.A: The payment is from taxes paid by employed workers.
options.B: The payment is made from government savings not current income.
options.C: The payment is made without the production of goods and services taking place.
options.D: The payment must be spent as directed by the government.

questions.questionText: What describes a regressive tax?

options.A: low income earners pay a higher proportion of their income in tax than high income earners
options.B: marginal tax rates exceed average tax rates
options.C: the cost of collecting the tax exceeds the revenue raised
options.D: the marginal rate of tax is higher for high income earners than for low income earners

questions.questionText: A government is concerned that foreign-owned companies are responsible for a high proportion of the economy’s output. Therefore it nationalises timber extraction, which is controlled by a foreign-owned company. What benefit will the economy gain from the change in ownership?

options.A: forestry workers will become the new owners
options.B: profits will no longer be sent abroad to foreign shareholders
options.C: social costs arising from forestry will be eliminated
options.D: the market for timber will become more competitive

questions.questionText: What will definitely lead to an improvement in the terms of trade?

options.A: Export prices fall whilst import prices rise.
options.B: Export prices rise by the same amount as import prices.
options.C: Export prices rise slower than import prices.
options.D: Export prices rise whilst import prices stay the same.

The diagram shows the value of the Nigerian naira against the US dollar between June 2015 and June 2016. naira per 260 dollar June June 2015 2016 Which term is used for the change in the value of the naira in June 2016?

options.A: appreciation
options.B: depreciation
options.D: revaluation

questions.questionText: Countries M and N produce the world supply of machines and textiles. The table shows what each country produces when it divides its resources equally between the two products. machines textiles country M 1000 500 country N 900 300 total 1900 800 What should happen according to the principle of comparative advantage?

options.A: Country M should produce both machines and textiles.
options.B: Country M should specialise in the production of machines, country N should specialise in production of textiles.
options.C: Country M should specialise in the production of textiles, country N should specialise in production of machines.
options.D: Country N should produce both machines and textiles.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an aggregate supply curve, and aggregate demand curves. AS price level AD AD O national income What would cause a decrease in aggregate demand from AD to AD ?
Two countries trade with one another without any forms of protection. They also impose a common external tariff on the imports from all other countries. What have these two countries formed?

options.A: a customs union
options.B: a free trade area
options.D: an economic union

questions.questionText: The terms of trade of a developing country fell from 90 in 2010 to 80 in 2015. Assuming the index of its import prices remained constant at 110 between these two years, what happened to its index of export prices?

options.A: fell by 10
options.B: fell by 11
options.D: increased by 30

questions.questionText: Which type of import control allows a country to develop a potential comparative advantage in a particular good?

options.A: a quota that protects jobs in a depressed region
options.B: a short-term tariff that protects an infant industry
options.C: a tariff that improves an industry’s terms of trade
options.D: an embargo on goods with negative externalities

questions.questionText: The diagram shows aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) in an economy. The initial equilibrium is at point E. AS AS AS price W 2 P level 1 E P X P AD O national output What causes shifts in the aggregate supply curve from AS to AS and from AS to AS ?
Which action might be part of an expansionary economic policy?

options.A: reducing the budget deficit
options.B: reducing the level of government spending
options.D: reducing the rate of interest

questions.questionText: A government is faced with rising inflation. It wishes to reduce inflationary pressure while avoiding a fall in output. Which action is most likely to meet its needs?

options.A: an increase in laws to promote competition
options.B: an increase in taxation
options.C: an increase in the budget surplus
options.D: an increase in the exchange rate

questions.questionText: Why may a government seek to reduce a current account surplus on the balance of payments?

options.A: to lower inflation
options.B: to lower unemployment
options.C: to raise the economic growth rate
